text:
maria: heads-up — saw a burst of HPA-driven scale today in eu-west2 that triggered cluster-autoscaler to add 4 GPU nodes and then pods sat in ContainerCreating for ~4m. suspect CNI or network egress quotas. anyone else seeing it? :thinking_face:
raj: saw that too. k8s events show 'FailedAttachVolume' and some CNI rate-limit warnings. CA metrics show rapid add then scale down.
taylor: hmm, are the pods pending on attaching an fs or just image pull/timeouts?
maria: mostly image pulls + init containers hitting 429 from our private registry (eu registry). also a few `FailedAttachVolume` for gpu-local-scratch. logs: `cni: rate limit exceeded`, `imagepuller: 429 Too Many Requests`.
kai: this is classic warm-pool mismatch + autoscaler surge. GPU pool has taint `gpu-only: true:NoSchedule` and warm nodes are tainted differently, so HPA spins up on gpu pool while warm nodes in general pool aren't used. CA then requests new gpu nodes.
raj: short-term mitigation: debounce the HPA signal and add an external metrics rolling window. example PromQL we use for smoothing:```
avg_over_time(queue_length_total{job="queue-exporter",env="prod"}[30s])
```
raj: and HPA can reference an externally computed metric so we avoid per-second spikes. also add `--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-downscale-stabilization` on controller manager if needed.
taylor: can we also throttle image pulls from registry by adding `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent` + ensure node image cache warm pool has pre-pulled images?
maria: pre-pulled images would help but requires warm GPU nodes with same OS/images. that's expensive. maybe short-term: increase registry quota for eu region (we have a soft quota). asked infra team to lift it for 30m.
infra-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler@gke: scaled up 4 nodes in nodepool gpu-eu-west2 at 2026-03-17T15:12:03Z
sre-oncall: btw CA config has `--expander=least-waste` which favors launching specialized gpu nodes. we could switch to `numeric` or tweak scale-up-delay to avoid oscillation. also CA's `--max-node-provision-time` may be set low, causing repeated retries.
kai: CA flags we should consider (example):```
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
--max-node-provision-time=20m
--balance-similar-node-groups
```
maria: another factor: VPA was active on some inf pods and suggested memory increases; VPA recommender triggered evictions during the window which made the HPA see higher QPS per pod -> more replicas -> CA reaction. we should freeze VPA recommendations for gpu workloads during peak.
raj: agreed. quick HPA annotation to debounce: `autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: '{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":120,"policies":[{"type":"Percent","value":100,"periodSeconds":15}]},"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300}}'`
taylor: that annotation looks right. Also suggest using external-metrics adapter with `window=1m` for queue metrics.
sre-oncall: action items: 1) add HPA debounce annotation to affected deployments (maria/taylor) — done as interim. 2) request temporary lift of registry quota for eu region (maria) — pending. 3) change CA expander to numeric for gpu pool & increase scale-down delay (kai to propose PR). 4) pause VPA updates for gpu namespaces during peak (raj to coordinate).
maria: I'll post the HPA patch now and monitor. thanks. :thumbsup:
kai: I'll open the CA flag change PR and include a small experiment to flip expander for 15m & observe.
raj: leaving a note: long-term we should add an autoscaler-aware warm-pool that matches taints + pre-pulled images, and an image registry mirror in eu-west2. reduces cross-region egress and pull bursts.
taylor: putting that on the infra roadmap.
infra-bot: [note] incident-log created: #INC-2026-0317-gpu-scale-network-throttle
maria: monitoring update — p95 latency back to normal after HPA debounce applied. leaving thread open for CA PR follow-ups.
